old: Picture a city's old defenses — this word once named the sturdy wall built to keep enemies out.
Its ancestor meant 'rampart' in Middle French, before the word crossed into English wearing a more elegant coat.
It shares a Germanic root with 'bulwark' — same defensive stone, two different doors into English.
clues: This name for a kind of city street began life as a word for a defensive rampart, a fortress wall built to keep enemies out.
It is a broad city thoroughfare, wider and grander than a typical avenue, often lined with trees. Many were laid out where old fortifications once stood.
Sunset in Los Angeles is a famous one, and the word shares its Germanic root with bulwark, a word that still means a protective wall.
